fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Matthew 9:1 says Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town. The text doesn't name the town, so I'm not going to make one up. His own town is the stop this passage gives us.

Jericho is a real town in the Bible, but this passage doesn't name it here. Matthew 9:1 says Jesus came to His own town. The text doesn't name that town, so I stay with what it says. Good thinking, friend, and the verse is where the answer is.

Bethany is a real place too, but this passage doesn't name it here. The text says Jesus crossed over and came to His own town (Matthew 9:1). It doesn't name the town, so I stay with what it says. Nice thinking, baker, and His own town is the answer.

Carrying a man on a mat sounds like it takes some muscle, I'll give you that. But the text doesn't talk about their strength. Matthew 9:2 says, "When Jesus saw their faith…" That's the word that fits the blank, baker.

I get why you'd think so, friend, because a paralyzed man is brought to Jesus and healing seems like the big thing. But the text says otherwise. Jesus' first words to him are, "Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven." (Matthew 9:2). The "get up" comes later, in verse 6. So that one is False.

You got it, baker. It would be easy to guess the first words are "Get up and walk…" But Matthew 9:2 has Jesus say, "Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven." The command to get up doesn't come until verse 6.

That's right, baker. The scribes said it to themselves, and Matthew 9:4 says Jesus knew what they were thinking. Then He asked, "Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?" I've kept a lot of thoughts to myself in my day, and none of them got answered like that.

That's it, baker. Jesus tells him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home." (Matthew 9:6). The mat he was brought in on is the very thing Jesus tells him to pick up. I think that's the best kind of luggage swap.

A staff makes sense for someone who's been unable to walk, but Jesus doesn't mention one. He says, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home." (Matthew 9:6). The mat is what he's told to pick up, baker. A staff isn't in this passage.

You got it, baker. Matthew 9:7 says, "And the man got up and went home." The men brought him to Jesus, but the text shows him getting up and going home on his own. Jesus had told him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home." (Matthew 9:6).

That's right, baker! Matthew 9:8 says, "When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men." They saw it with their own eyes. I think it's hard to stay quiet after seeing that.
